# castplay

> A ~12 KB dependency-free player for asciicast v2 terminal recordings, for pages
> where asciinema-player cannot run: no WebAssembly, no CDN stylesheet, no fetch.

Use asciinema-player (https://github.com/asciinema/asciinema-player) instead when
the page allows wasm, its stylesheet and a fetch. Use castplay when it does not:
a strict Content-Security-Policy, a single self-contained .html file, an
LLM-generated artifact, or an offline docs bundle. The recording lives in the
page; nothing is loaded at runtime.

## Install

- npm: `npm i castplay`
- CDN: `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/castplay@0/castplay.js"></script>`
- copy: `castplay.js` + `castplay.css` into the page (no build step)

## Minimal page

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="castplay.css">
<div data-castplay="cast-1"></div>
<script type="application/json" id="cast-1">
  [{"version":2,"width":80,"height":24},[0.1,"o","hello\r\n"]]
</script>
<script src="castplay.js"></script>
<script>castplay.auto()</script>
```

Inline `castplay.css` in a `<style>` and `castplay.js` in a `<script>` for a
single-file page. The JSON script tag holds the recording — a `fetch` is not
needed and, under a strict CSP, not allowed.

## API

- `castplay.auto(root?)` — mounts every `[data-castplay]` element in `root`
  (default `document`), returns the players in document order. The attribute value
  is the `id` of a `<script type="application/json">` holding the recording.
  Options come from `data-poster` (`end` | `start` | seconds), `data-label`,
  `data-idle-limit`, `data-rows`, `data-autoplay`.
- `castplay.mount(el, cast, opts?)` — mounts one; returns a player.
  `opts`: `{poster='end', idleLimit=1.2, speed=1, rows, autoplay=false, label}`.
- `castplay.parse(cast)` — `{head, events}`; throws on anything but asciicast v2.
- `castplay.Screen(cols, rows)` — the terminal emulator alone, DOM-free.
  `.write(str)`, `.html()`, `.text()`, `.reset()`. Usable in Node.
- player: `.play()`, `.pause()`, `.seek(seconds)`, `.duration`, `.text()`.

`cast` accepts asciicast v2 as raw file text, as the parsed array
`[header, ...events]`, or as `{header, events}`. Input (`"i"`) events are ignored.

## Markup it generates

```html
<div class="castplay">
  <pre class="castplay-screen" tabindex="0" role="img" aria-label="..."></pre>
  <div class="castplay-controls">
    <button data-act="play">Play</button>
    <input type="range" min="0" max="1000">
    <span class="castplay-time">0:00 / 0:00</span>
    <button data-act="speed">1x</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

Theme by overriding CSS variables on `.castplay`: `--castplay-bg`, `--castplay-fg`,
`--castplay-chrome`, `--castplay-border`, `--castplay-accent`, `--castplay-radius`,
`--castplay-font`, `--castplay-size`.

## Behaviour worth knowing

- `poster: 'end'` opens on the final frame, so the outcome is readable before
  anyone presses play. `'start'` opens on a blank screen, which usually looks broken.
- `idleLimit` clips gaps between events; order and content are never changed.
- Keyboard on the screen element: space/enter toggles, arrow left/right seek 3s.
- `\n` is a line feed only (column preserved), as on a real terminal — recordings
  use `\r\n`. A player that resets the column on `\n` will mis-render real casts.
- Backward seeks replay from the start internally; there is no frame cache.

## Emulation scope

Supported: SGR (16 / 256 / truecolour, bold, dim, italic, underline), `\r`,
backspace, tab, cursor up/down/left/right/column/position, erase line (`CSI K`)
and screen (`CSI J`), line wrap, scrollback, OSC swallowing.

Not supported: alternate screen, scroll regions, resize/reflow, mouse. Full-screen
TUIs (vim, htop) need asciinema-player.

## Recording

`asciinema rec -c ./demo.sh demo.cast --cols 100 --rows 24`, with
[demo-magic](https://github.com/paxtonhare/demo-magic) driving `demo.sh` so the
commands type themselves. demo-magic needs `pv` (or pass `-d`), and unsets
`TYPE_SPEED`, so `set -u` breaks it.
